source.note: Figures describe the Espace Killy (Tignes–Val d'Isère), the area covered by the standard day pass. Search summary of seevaldisere.com, Wikipedia and ski-pass pages: Espace Killy (Tignes–Val d'Isère, one ticket): 300 km of marked pistes; 90 lifts = 2 funiculars, 4 cable cars, 4 gondolas, 44 chairlifts, 36 surface lifts; one result states that '87 ski lifts' uplift 64,480 skiers and snowboarders per hour (likely an older lift count). Runs: 22 green, 68 blue, 39 red, 26 black (155). Val d'Isère's own lifts: 42, mostly chairlifts, including 15 drag lifts. Val d'Isère's own piste km not found.

character: Val d'Isère is a high village at the head of the Tarentaise valley that shares the Espace Killy with Tignes: about 300 km of pistes and around 90 lifts on one ticket. It is known for a long season, the Bellevarde runs and extensive off-piste terrain.
learning: The Espace Killy has 22 green and 68 blue runs (search summary), but much of it is high and exposed. Reference: Val d'Isère has beginner zones near the village; confirm beginner-lift access and ski-school options for 2026-27.
